items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: And Sharky organized this band, and all of a sudden we were just one huge hit.

ctx.x: Drove you crazy with all that kind of stuff. This is the third reel on it. Los Angeles country. I didn't hear what you were saying. I was setting the machine up. Pam asked you about big name entertainment here. They used to have more of it. There used to be more big name entertainment.

You see, the thing about it was when we and Tony Almerico's band brought the jazz back. Actually, Tony Almerico had it before we were, but he only played on Sunday afternoon at the Parisian Room. With all the guys like Roy, what's your name, on piano, and Shorty Reese on tenor, and Frank Federico, and all of them. Actually, Julian Lane played trombone. They only played on Sundays, but Tony was playing dances all over this country. And Sharky organized this band, and all of a sudden we were just one huge hit. And…
You got something from the item here on page 17, October the 18th, 1950.

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: Poor Santo, when we were playing with Sharky, you know, we made up to five hundred dollars a week with Sharky.

ctx.x: Well, you couldn't spend any money on the boat, huh, Much? No. Did you gamble? Oh, no. I never gambled. I would think that'd be one thing to do on the boats, river boats. That's traditional.

When I was playing with Tony Foucherat and Mutt Powers and Flavor Ford, like I told you, we were playing in Smack Over Arkansas at one time. No. Tony wasn't in that band. I was with Happy Cook and Little Chink Martin, Charlie DuPont, Harry Shields. When we were playing at a gambling place about five miles out of Smack Over Arkansas, when gambling was strictly against the law, on New Year's Eve night, I saw a man walk out after losing everything in the world he had. I couldn't get to him in time. He blew his…
